pages.text: The home base of a drone. Each dock hosts $(l)one drone$() and:$(br)$(li)$(l)charges$() it (up to 500 FE/t) from its own 100,000 FE buffer;$(br)$(li)$(l)stores$() the harvest in 9 slots;

$(li)remembers the drone's $(l)work area$();$(br)$(li)holds an $(l)item filter$() for the Quarry and Transport modules.$(br)Power the dock with a $(l:generators/combustion_generator)Combustion Generator$(/l) placed next to it, or with cables from any mod. The harvest can be pulled out with hoppers or item pipes from any side.

You can read a dock at a glance: lights $(l)chase round its landing ring$() while a drone flies home, and $(l)arcs of energy$() jump from its corner beacons to a drone charging on it. On a Builder Swarm Dock each of the four landing rings $(l)lights up$() while a Mini Drone stands on it.

Right-click the dock to open it:$(br)$(li)$(l)Drone Work$(): what the drone is doing right now (Harvesting, Quarrying, Transporting, Charging, Returning, On hold...).$(br)$(li)$(l)Drone Position$(): where the drone is, or $(l)Docked$() when it is on the pad.
pages.title: The dock screen

pages.text: $(li)The $(l)9 cargo slots$(), the $(l)Filter$() button (see below) and the dock's energy bar.$(br)$(li)$(l)Return / Resume$(): $(l)Return$() calls the drone home and keeps it there, charging but taking no new jobs (a Taxi drone first finishes the trip it is on). $(l)Resume$() lets it work again.
Two $(l)side tabs$() on the left open a panel next to the screen; click a tab again to close it. The screen remembers which one you left open.

$(li)$(l)Drone Status$() (the "i" tab, coloured like the drone's state): its state, the modules it carries, the work area (not for Transport and Taxi drones, which never use it) and, for Transport and Taxi drones, whether a route or a destination is set.
$(li)$(l)Battery$() (the battery tab, showing the charge): the charge level, the FE stored and whether the drone is charging or flying.

The $(item)Survey Tool$() sets up a dock. It has $(l)four modes$(): hold it and $(l)sneak + scroll the mouse wheel$() to switch, or $(l)right-click the air$() to go to the next one. The current mode shows above the hotbar and in the tooltip, and a click only does what that mode says. The tool never opens the
pages.title: The Survey Tool

pages.text: blocks you click, so chests and machines stay closed while you set things up.$(br)$(li)$(l)**Dock$()**: a Drone Dock: the tool now configures that dock. Sneak + right-click resets it.$(br)$(li)$(l)**Area$()**: two opposite corners: the dock's work area.

$(li)$(l)**Route$()**: two containers, source then destination: the transport route.$(br)$(li)$(l)**Taxi$()**: the block where taxi passengers land.$(br)The tool $(l)tells you each step$() above the hotbar: when you switch mode and after every click it says what to click next ("Click the source container", "Click the opposite corner"...).

The first click, in any mode, picks the dock you want to set up; after that a click does what the mode says. Dock mode only picks the dock (use it to switch to another dock): to connect the dock to a chest, use $(l)Route$() mode.

Without any setup the drone works a $(l)9x9$() area centred on the dock. To change it:$(br)$(li)Switch the tool to $(l)Area$() mode and $(l)right-click the dock$().$(br)$(li)$(l)Right-click the first corner$() of your field.$(br)$(li)$(l)Right-click the opposite corner$(). The dock now uses that area.
pages.title: Choosing the work area

pages.text: The area can be up to $(l)33x33$() blocks, the two corners can be at most $(l)8 blocks$() apart in height, and everything must stay within 48 blocks of the dock.
The drone works its area $(l)block by block from one corner to the other$(), row after row like a Quarry, so a field is harvested and replanted in order instead of here and there.

For drones with a $(l:drone_systems/modules)Transport Module$(/l):$(br)$(li)Switch the tool to $(l)Route$() mode and $(l)right-click the dock$().$(br)$(li)$(l)Right-click the source container$() (chest, barrel, any modded inventory, or $(l)another drone's dock$()).
pages.title: Setting a transport route

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Right-click the destination container$(). The route is saved on the dock.$(br)Both must be within $(l)48 blocks of the dock$(), and their chunks loaded: an $(l:drone_systems/addons)Anchor Addon$(/l) keeps them so.
Another drone's Drone Dock counts as a container: a Transport drone can empty the dock of a Harvester or a Quarry and bring the harvest to your storage.

For drones with a $(l:drone_systems/modules)Taxi Module$(/l): with the tool linked to the dock, switch to $(l)Taxi$() mode and $(l)right-click the block$() where passengers should land. It can be up to 256 blocks away and needs two blocks of air above it.
pages.title: Setting a taxi destination

pages.text: The $(l)Filter$() button under the dock's slots opens its filter:$(br)$(li)with a $(l:drone_systems/modules)Quarry Module$(/l), the drone $(l)keeps only the drops that pass$() and throws the rest away (e.g. a whitelist of ores, or a blacklist of cobblestone, dirt and gravel);
pages.title: Item filter

pages.text: $(li)with a $(l:drone_systems/modules)Transport Module$(/l), the drone $(l)moves only the items that pass$().$(br)Click a slot with an item to add it as a sample (nothing is used up), click it empty-handed to clear it. The buttons switch between $(l)whitelist$() and $(l)blacklist$(), match items $(l)exactly$() (enchantments, damage, names) or

not, match $(l)by mod$(), and pick a $(l)tag$() of the first sample (e.g. #forge:ores). An empty blacklist, the default, lets everything through.$(br2)The bottom row sets a $(l)limit$() for the Transport Module: $(l)Keep at destination: N$(). The drone then stops bringing an item once the destination holds

N of it, and carries only what is missing, so a chest stays stocked with 64 bread instead of filling up with 2,000. The arrows step through round numbers (8, 16, 32 and on up to 4,096); hold $(l)Shift$() to step by one. It counts each item separately.

$(li)$(l)Sneak + right-click in the air$() clears a corner or route source you set by mistake (switching mode clears it too).$(br)$(li)In $(l)Dock$() mode, $(l)sneak + right-click the dock$() resets it: default 9x9 area, no transport route, no taxi destination.
pages.title: Fixing mistakes
Builder Swarm Dock
pages.text: A dock for up to $(l)four Mini Drones$() (drones built on a $(l:drone_systems/drone_frames)Mini Drone Frame$(/l)). They share its work area, transport route, build and stock, and each parks on its own corner of the pad. Four $(l:drone_systems/modules)Builder$(/l) Mini Drones raise a

structure together: link it to the swarm dock with the Multiblock Projector, and they split its blocks between them.$(br)$(li)Right-click the swarm dock with a Mini Drone to deploy it; it takes up to four. Bigger drones do not fit, and Mini Drones do not fit an ordinary Drone Dock.
$(li)The screen shows the swarm as one: the busiest drone's job, their batteries added up, and how many drones are on the dock.
The $(l:drone_systems/hologram_table)Hologram Table$(/l) shows all your docks and drones on a 3D map.
